title: ZDI publishes 0-day advisory on pip configuration file permissions (ZDI-26-1066)
date_note: Coordinated public release date stated on the ZDI advisory.
summary: The Zero Day Initiative published advisory ZDI-26-1066 (CVE-2026-136440) on 24 November 2026 for a local privilege escalation flaw in pip caused by incorrect permissions on configuration files. ZDI rates it CVSS 7.3 and says the attacker needs low-privileged code execution and user interaction. ZDI says the vendor rejected the report on 3 May 2025, and the advisory names no fix.
plain: ZDI disclosed a flaw in the Python tool pip where configuration file permissions could let a local attacker gain higher privileges. ZDI says the vendor rejected the report and names no fix.
exec: ZDI rates the pip flaw CVSS 7.3 and names no vendor fix; the vendor rejected the report, per ZDI.
action: ZDI's only stated mitigation is to restrict interaction with the product; the advisory names no vendor patch.

validation.note: Only the ZDI advisory was read; it is the researcher's own primary page.

review.note: Compared CVE, CVSS 7.3, local low-priv, rejection 3 May 2025, mitigation, date with ZDI
